details:
Most users I encounter tend to use avatars from avatar worlds. These avatars, while sometimes annoying, are mostly harmless and fall in line with VRChat ToS. While many private avatar users follow community guidelines as well, many others use private avatars to crash VRChat clients or display shocking/obscene content (images of dead bodies, pornography, Klan outfits, etc), which disturbs a comfortable gameplay experience.
While blocking exists, it is only effective *after* the user has experienced the shocking/obscene content (or, in the case of crashers, is difficult or impossible if the crasher's name is unknown) and only works on the individual level. The Safety settings also already exist, but blocking all avatars from New Users would block the majority of public avatar users.
To remedy this, a toggle could be implemented to hide avatars that have been uploaded directly to another user's account rather than being cloned in a public world or obtained from a public pedestal. This feature, while generally welcome to the average user, would be extra useful for streamers (who don't want to get a Twitch/YT/FB ban) and Quest users (who are frequently targeted for crashers). The toggle would be placed as either a checkbox under the Avatar button in the Safety menu or an indented checkbox in Settings under Streamer Mode (making it a required feature of Streamer Mode would interfere with streamers who exclusively play in private areas).
An argument could be made that this setting would only kick the can down the road. Sure, crashers and trolls would be easily dealt with, but instead of manually enabling avatars for each Visitor and New User, you'd now have to manually enable private avatars for every non-troll, including Trusted Users. This is true, but the same argument can be (and was) made against the Safety system. What's more, if the feature is implemented as part of the Safety system, it will allow for a finer level of control that would require *less* manual interference.
***TL;DR:*** Private/less-public avatars are subject to less scrutiny, and therefore exploited by trolls to ruin experiences (crashers, shock/gore, Klan promotion, etc). Blocking is not always effective, and hiding all New Users cuts out a large portion of the player base (given how long it takes to reach User status). An option to hide private/less-public avatars could be added as a sub-option of the Avatar button in Safety settings to allow a finer level of control over user experiences without an inconvenient amount of effort.
title: Toggle to show/hide privately uploaded/non-public avatars
